              else if (editHollow) { opts.learningSink?.alphaBetaDelta.push(await penaliseHollowTemplate("feature_compose", "landed-edit-missing-requested-symbol")); }
              recordDeterministicLabel(goal ?? "", earlyLandedSha ? `feature_compose:${earlyLandedSha}` : undefined, "feature_compose", { reached: earlyReached, reason: `deterministic:early-edit-intent-${earlyReached ? "landed" : "not-landed"}${earlyLandedSha ? ` ${earlyLandedSha}` : ""}`, deterministic: true });
              return {

The first and third lines are unchanged and must be reproduced exactly; only the middle line is new. Change nothing else anywhere in the file.

CRITICAL PLACEMENT CONSTRAINT: the new statement goes AFTER the complete if / else-if chain and immediately BEFORE the return. It must NOT be placed between the preceding `if (!earlyLandedSha) { ... }` line and the `else if (editHollow) { ... }` line. Inserting there severs the if/else chain and the file fails to parse with 'Unexpected else' — that exact regression crash-looped this vessel earlier today. Performing this as a two-line replacement, with the else-if line reproduced verbatim as the first line of the replacement, is what makes that outcome impossible.

WHY: this is the EARLY edit-intent completion path. It grades correctly — earlyReached requires a real landing sha AND a post-state check that the requested symbol is present — but it returns without ever calling recordDeterministicLabel, so its outcome reaches the oracle corpus through no path at all. Its sibling, the routed edit-intent path, already has this call; the reconciliation path at ~16163 has had it for longer. Leaving only the early path uncredited makes the corpus biased BY ROUTE: whether a goal is graded would depend on whether the walk had already started, which is unrelated to the goal's merit, and that bias feeds Thompson posteriors and ribosome extraction.

All identifiers are already in scope at that point: goal, earlyLandedSha, earlyReached. The call records BOTH polarities — a not-landed outcome is labelled not_achieved exactly as faithfully as a landing is labelled achieved — so it makes the corpus complete rather than more favourable. Grading is untouched.
